name: Cassia obovata (neutral henna)

card.summary: A colourless plant powder from senna leaves, used as a conditioning hair treatment that adds shine and body without adding red henna colour.
card.note: Pale or bleached hair can pick up a golden tint; products sold as neutral henna may differ in contents.

quick.overview:
Cassia obovata, sold as neutral henna, is a powder made from the leaflets of a senna plant. Despite the name it is not true henna; it is used as a conditioning treatment that gives hair a smoother, glossier look without the orange-red dye of henna.

A 1981 laboratory study found that its components bind to hair keratin, and that bleached and light hair took on a golden light-brown tone while dark hair showed no uptake. People also mix it with henna to get lighter reds and blonds.
quick.how: The dry powder is mixed with water into a paste, applied to hair, left for a period and rinsed, commonly as a conditioning mask or blended with henna and indigo for colour variation.
quick.risks: Natural henna products are generally considered low-risk for hair, but products sold as henna can contain other ingredients, and black henna may contain PPD, a strong allergen. People with G6PD deficiency are at risk with henna.

lead: Cassia obovata, commonly sold as neutral henna, is a powder from the leaflets of a senna plant (often also named Senna italica). It is used as a hair conditioner that adds shine and body without the red-orange colour of true henna, and is blended with henna to lighten reds toward blond.[2][3]

A 1981 paper in the International Journal of Cosmetic Science described it as a cosmetic wrongly called neutral henna, traditionally used as a laxative and in the Middle Ages blended with henna as "the two hennas".[4] The study reported that components of the powder fix to keratin, and that bleached hair turned golden light-brown while dark hair showed no diffusion.[4]

chain: Hair looks glossier and fuller, with a golden tint on light hair
angle.text: People use it as a colourless conditioning mask for smoother, shinier hair. On bleached or light hair it can leave a golden tint, and mixed with henna it shifts reds lighter.

infobox: None to golden on light hair

paras: Neutral henna is milled senna leaf rather than Lawsonia inermis, the true henna plant.[2][3] It does not change colour on dark hair in the way henna does, though product contents vary.[2]

Users apply it as a paste to condition and thicken the look of hair, and combine it with henna for lighter reds or with indigo for browns.[2] The 1981 study found uptake of its components followed diffusion into the hair and was fastest in bleached hair (7.5 percent uptake in 9 hours), with none in dark hair.[4]
No studies found of its effect on hair appearance in people. A 1981 laboratory study examined uptake by hair samples,[4] and a 2022 study examined its use as a textile dye.[5]

Natural henna is generally considered low-risk for hair, though people with G6PD deficiency can have serious reactions.[2] Some products sold as henna contain metal salts or allergenic dyes, and black henna may contain para-phenylenediamine, which can cause lifelong sensitisation.[2]

timeline.event: Laboratory study describes Cassia obovata as the cosmetic known as neutral henna.[4]
